Latin word

etiam

adverb · Wiktionary

also, too; even; even; again, once more: more of doing something; yes (indeed)

In this lexicon

  • also

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. Ep. 8.8.6: īnfrā etiam natāre concessum; Cic. Tusc. 5.100: nōn sōlum in praesentiā, sed etiam posterō diē; Traupman 270

  • even

    the recommended word · classical · Publ. E 13: Etiam capillus ūnus habet umbram suam.; Plin. Ep. 6.20.18: sōl etiam effulsit; Traupman 310

  • more

    also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 2.2.43: Circumspice etiam (Lewis & Short)

  • yes

    also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 544–544b: numquid vīs? — Etiam: ut āctūtum adveniās.; Cic. Ac. 2.104: aut etiam aut nōn respondēre possit; Traupman 67, 410

  • etiam atque etiam: emphasize

    classical

Examples

  • Valē. — Et tū; numquid vīs aliud?

    Goodbye. — You too. Is there anything else you want?Ter. Eun. 190–191
